newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian Feb retail trade shrinks 0.2 pct mth/mth.
newsitem.headline: Croatian Feb retail trade shrinks 0.2 pct mth/mth.

text.p: Croatian retail trade shrank 0.2 percent in February from January, while rising 29.9 percent from the year-ago month, the State Statistics Bureau reported on Wednesday.
It put January-February retail sales 31 percent higher than in the same period of 1996.
February stocks rose 0.6 percent on a monthly level and 12.1 percent from February last year as retail sales in most branches decreased slightly.
Specialised shops were the only ones recording a monthly turnover rise of an average nine percent last month due to seasonal sales of goods such as clothes and footwear.
The biggest decline was by 6.2 percent at non-specialised retailers.
March retail sales were forecast to rise 11 percent by some 500 leading retailers, representing more than a half of the total domestic trade sector.

Gross sales rose a meagre 0.2 percent in February from January and 14.4 percent year-on-year. They were seen as growing a further 6.7 percent in March. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
